open_obligations.what_is_open: A common-fiber-preserving realization of the purification program that maps every residual catalog entry to a diagonal unit-residual entry while weakly increasing both common support and affine score at every admissible pair of margins, together with a two-way equality characterization.
open_obligations.obstruction: The available pure-profile reduction is one-dimensional and does not preserve a prescribed joint buyer--seller subset-sum fiber. The residual-copy comparison used by optimizer containment preserves the relevant support only while replacing one side by a copy of the other side's residual coordinates; it does not split arbitrary paired residual coordinates into diagonal unit coordinates. Consequently it supplies neither the required universal map into \(\mathcal U_R\) nor the score comparison and equality conditions for all \(n_B,n_S\ge 4R\).
open_obligations.attempted: The support-preserving residual-copy route and the proposed LYM/unit-rank route were compared with the stated purification handle. The former proves finite residual concentration but does not perform the required unit-coordinate elementary compressions. The latter controls ranks in a single subset-sum poset but does not control the intersection of the two weighted target fibers, so its injections need not preserve the common bivariate fiber. Neither route yields the simultaneous inequalities or their equality cases.

prose_updates.tldr: For independently and uniformly half-randomized populations on two unequal market sides, the optimal covering rectangle at a required support \(R\) is reduced to a finite residual catalog depending only on \(R\). For \(R\ge 4\) and \(n_B,n_S\ge 4R\), the exact frontier is the maximum of finitely many affine catalog scores, and the phase inequalities retain every catalog tie. A constant-incidence sampler implements the selected event, and null-adjusted focal outcomes yield exact one-sided inversion for a sharp constant total effect. No universal collapse of the catalog to diagonal unit residuals is claimed.

project_justification.gap: The closest exact two-sided-market method proves validity for selected equal blocks and treats block choice heuristically; general biclique methods establish validity and power guidance but do not classify the optimal covering paired rectangle. Existing one-dimensional subset-sum purification does not preserve a prescribed common buyer--seller target fiber.
project_justification.niche: Balanced independent randomization converts admissible covering rectangles into two coupled half-sum profiles. This structure permits an exact finite residual reduction and affine phase analysis while retaining unequal market-side sizes, without asserting an unrestricted-biclique optimum.
project_justification.fill: A two-stage concentration argument bounds the residual on the smaller side and uses a support-preserving residual-copy comparison to bound the larger residual. This yields a finite catalog, an exact affine frontier with all catalog ties, an implementable conditional law, and exact one-sided sharp-null inversion. Whether every catalog entry can be purified to a dominating diagonal unit-residual entry remains a separate open question.

prose_updates.related_work: Liu, Shaikh, and Toulis (2026) establish the equal \(k\)-block total-effect test and motivate the support--focal-size trade-off; the present result optimizes over covering paired rectangles through a finite residual catalog. Puelz, Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2022) encode imputable tests as bicliques and motivate large bicliques, but do not supply the paired-rectangle classification. Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) provide the conditioning-mechanism validity theorem used after imputability is verified. Basse, Ding, Feller, and Toulis (2024) provide the orbit-equivariance template, while unequal rectangular profiles require a separate constant-incidence count. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu (2021) provide discrete Fisher inversion machinery, specialized here after null-adjusted dyadic imputability and crossing monotonicity are established. Singhal (2019) motivates bilinear subset-sum profiles and one-dimensional purification, but does not furnish a coupled common-fiber-preserving reduction to diagonal unit residuals. Ye et al. (2023) provide the unequal-side marketplace consumer through Platform O's independent user-view and ad randomizations.
prose_updates.interpretation: The finite-catalog result is the actionable design certificate: for fixed resolution \(R\), one enumerates \(\mathcal C_R\), evaluates the affine scores at the observed pair of market sizes, and retains every maximizer on a phase boundary. The unresolved unit-residual question concerns only whether this already finite computation admits a further universal closed-form collapse; it is not needed for catalog optimality, sampling, or exact one-sided inversion.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The conditioning event must be selected without outcomes. Raw focal outcomes are not imputable under a nonzero sharp constant effect, so the null-adjusted array \(Q_\tau\) is essential. Complement symmetry implies that an ordinary nonrandomized absolute-score test has minimum \(p\)-value at least \(2/h(a,b)\), so support \(20\) cannot support an ordinary two-sided test at level \(0.05\). In addition, the finite catalog has not been proved to collapse universally to the diagonal unit-residual subcatalog: known one-dimensional purification arguments do not preserve the required joint buyer--seller target fiber.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves the finite residual catalog, exact affine frontier and catalog equality cases, constant-incidence sampler, and exact one-sided inversion under the sharp constant total-effect null. Universal unit-residual purification remains an explicit unresolved question and is not used by those results. The note makes no claim about weak-null validity, power or confidence-width optimality, unrestricted bicliques, minimality of the \(4R\) threshold, ordinary two-sided \(95\)-percent inversion at support \(20\), or the empirical validity of the constant-effect exposure model for Platform O.

statement_notes.justification: A positive answer would replace the certified finite catalog computation by a smaller diagonal unit-residual search and could expose a closed all-resolution extremal mechanism, but it is not needed for the proved affine frontier.
statement_notes.gap: Neither the support-preserving residual-copy comparison nor a one-dimensional LYM/unit-rank reduction realizes the required elementary compression while preserving the chosen common bivariate fiber. Simultaneous support dominance, affine-score dominance for all admissible aspect ratios, and the equality cases therefore remain unproved.
statement_notes.consumer: Designers can already compute the exact optimum by finite catalog enumeration. Resolving this question would simplify that computation further, but no current implementation or validity claim depends on it.
